[TEMPORAL] User went to a hidden gem of a park last Sunday and saw a Yellow Warbler and a Black-and-white Warbler.  
[PREFERENCE] User is interested in birding and spotting warblers.  
[PREFERENCE] User's daughter loves coming to the park and has gotten good at spotting birds.  
[PREFERENCE] User's son is more into photography.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Congratulations on spotting your first Common Yellowthroat!  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Oakwood State Park has several woodland trails that are perfect for spotting warblers, including the Redbud Trail, Oak Trail, and Pine Trail.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Edge habitats where the forest meets open fields or wetlands can be hotspots for warblers.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] The streams and creeks within the park, such as the one along the Bluebird Trail, can attract warblers.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] User should try to arrive at the park early in the morning when birds are most active.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] User should listen for distinctive sounds of warblers to help with spotting.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] User should scan the canopy with binoculars to spot warblers.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] User should bring a field guide to help with warbler identification.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] In early spring, user may spot other migrant species like the Ruby-crowned Kinglet, Hermit Thrush, and White-throated Sparrow.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Oakwood State Park is a great spot for raptor sightings, including Red-tailed Hawks, Cooper's Hawks, and American Kestrels.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] User can create a scavenger hunt list with items like leaves, rocks, or specific bird species to engage their daughter.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] The park's Nature Center offers educational programs and exhibits that are perfect for kids.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] The bird feeder station near the Nature Center is an excellent spot for photography.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Areas with water, like streams, ponds, or wetlands, are good for bird photography.
